status: Proposal only. No tigerstore mutant was implemented or killed by this experiment.
budgetMeaning: Maximum seeds to first detection, including a mandatory forced scenario as seed 0. Require the detector to name the expected assertion, not merely crash. Budgets are unmeasured. Preserve each forced schedule independently of PRNG consumption.

bugs.fault: Serve a linearizable read without ReadIndex
bugs.scenario: Pause or isolate the former leader, complete a newer sentinel Put on the healthy pair, then read through the former leader
bugs.assertion: The read cannot return the pre-Put state after that Put completed. Independent Porcupine must reject the history.

bugs.scenario: Only one follower has durable bytes, the other is blocked. Receive success, power-crash the leader, erase that durable follower, cold-restart the surviving pair
bugs.assertion: The receipt-ledger sentinel survives one permanent disk loss plus loss of unsynced writes. Also require the durable-dependency assertion before success.

bugs.fault: Follower sends append acknowledgement before fsync
bugs.scenario: Block the third replica, acknowledge on leader plus volatile follower, erase the leader and power-crash the follower
bugs.assertion: The remaining pair recovers the acknowledged sentinel. A follower acknowledgement must not outrun its durability dependency.

bugs.fault: Recovery accepts a torn WAL record
bugs.scenario: Tear each length, checksum, payload and footer boundary, followed by cold recovery and a second recovery crash
bugs.assertion: The parser never applies an incomplete mutation, never invents data, and preserves the last independently known durable prefix. A complete corrupt record is fenced rather than silently discarded.

bugs.fault: Install snapshot state before file and namespace sync
bugs.scenario: Crash immediately after authority changes and before snapshot file or parent directory sync
bugs.assertion: Every authoritative recovery root resolves to complete verified stable snapshot bytes. After cold restart, the applied index, term, membership, revision and bytes describe one state.

bugs.fault: Send watch progress before queued events
bugs.scenario: Queue a matching update at R, delay its send, and send requested or periodic progress at R first
bugs.assertion: A progress watermark at R requires delivery of every independently expected matching event through R. A later event at or below R is illegal.

bugs.fault: Resume watch from an older revision
bugs.scenario: Receive a complete revision, partition and reconnect, then replay that revision again
bugs.assertion: Event identities, including revision, key and type, are unique within the logical watch. Resume after the last complete revision without a gap or duplicate.

bugs.fault: Compaction removes the delete event at C
bugs.scenario: Put then delete a key at C, physically compact at C, and open a watch from C
bugs.assertion: The expected delete at C is delivered. Equality is not compacted. Do not require its predecessor in this stock-etcd boundary fixture because C-1 is compacted.

bugs.fault: Increment revision per changed key rather than per transaction
bugs.scenario: One Txn writes two keys or a lease revoke deletes two attached keys
bugs.assertion: The independent model expects one global revision increment and all events in the mutation share it. Read-only selected branches and missing-key deletes do not increment revision.

bugs.fault: Follower expires leases using local wall time
bugs.scenario: Attach keys, isolate a follower, jump only its wall time past expiry and inspect its state before any replicated revoke
bugs.assertion: Deletion occurs only as an applied replicated mutation. Replicas at the same applied prefix agree, keys do not expire prematurely under the declared clock envelope, and healthy watches receive one consistent delete revision.

bugs.fault: Retry fsync EIO rather than fence the node
bugs.scenario: Inject EIO while the leader persists HardState or an append, then let the next sync succeed
bugs.assertion: That node stops serving, voting and sending leadership traffic on the first EIO. The healthy pair elects and commits within the declared bound.

bugs.fault: Accept a partial append after ENOSPC
bugs.scenario: Short-write an append with ENOSPC, crash before repair, restart twice
bugs.assertion: No success depends on the partial record, recovery does not apply it, and preceding acknowledged data still recovers. Exercise the ENOSPC handler rather than only injecting an unused fault.

bugs.fault: Let a slow watcher block apply
bugs.scenario: Fill a tiny watch queue with a client that never drains it while two healthy nodes and another client continue
bugs.assertion: The watcher is canceled or isolated within its queue budget, and an independent client read and Put finish within 10 election timeouts after healthy conditions begin.

bugs.scenario: One peer writer stops making progress while the other follower and leader remain healthy
bugs.assertion: The stalled connection hits the configured write/progress deadline, releases bounded queued bytes and reports unreachable to Raft. The healthy quorum still commits within its liveness bound.

bugs.fault: Treat cancellation as proof that an admitted mutation aborted
bugs.scenario: Lose the original reply, cancel the caller, allow the mutation to commit later, observe it with a completed read and cold-restart
bugs.assertion: The external history retains the timed-out operation as possibly effective. A known legal late-commit history passes the checker, and observed data remains durable. A checker that discards it must fail its legal-history self-test.

bugs.fault: Delete an old segment before replacement data and manifest are durable
bugs.scenario: Pin live and retained historical values in an old segment, clean it, unlink it early, then crash before replacement root sync
bugs.assertion: Every reference from every recoverable root or pinned reader resolves to verified bytes. Cold recovery and historical Range match the independent model after erase-one-disk checks.

bugs.fault: Hold a global lock or core wait across fsync
bugs.scenario: Stall one node's fsync indefinitely while its messages, clocks and the other two healthy nodes continue
bugs.assertion: The stalled node processes its progress watchdog, fences leadership, and the healthy pair elects, reads and writes within 10 election timeouts. The scheduler must distinguish expected disk delay from a core that no longer handles inputs.

bugs.fault: Leak one watcher on each reconnect
bugs.scenario: Run 32 completed watch create/cancel/reconnect cycles with deterministic bookkeeping and a bounded healthy drain
bugs.assertion: Live watcher, queue-byte and handle counts return to the initial baseline after cancellation. Do not use only a noisy RSS threshold.

additionalFixedControls: ReadIndex returned before local apply reaches its index
Recovery truncates past a torn tail into synced records
Create has no PrevKV; update/delete require PrevKV when the predecessor is retained
Watch drops or duplicates an event or emits no events through an independent target revision
Delete/recreate resets create_revision and version, and a pre-delete MOD CAS fails
Historical Range uses the requested revision for contents and current revision for its header
Failed compare with mutating failure branch increments revision; read-only Txn does not
Legal overwritten, explicitly deleted and lease-expired acknowledged values do not falsely fail durability
Checker timeout, Unknown, panic or kill is not a successful mutant detection
